types.name: FMLModels
types.doc:
The ML models (wav2vec2 for auto-subtitles, the PBRify texture models) are
~128 MB, so they live in an archive of their own instead of
EngineContent.meaf: MBT packs Engine/Source/Runtime/ML/Models into
MLModels.meaf beside the binaries, and a game package carries one only when
it opts into auto-subtitles (and then holds only the speech model). The
archive is optional — an install without it simply has no models.

members.name: kMountPoint
members.doc: The VFS prefix the models answer under: "Content/ML/ASR/…", "Content/ML/PBRify/…".

members.name: Mount
members.doc:
Mounts MLModels.meaf at kMountPoint the first time it is found beside
the executable, under its Content/ folder, under the game root's Content/
or in the working directory, and the source folder of a dev tree below
it. Cheap to call before every model read; true when the models are reachable.

members.name: SourceDirectory
members.doc: Engine/Source/Runtime/ML/Models in a source tree; empty when there is none.

types.name: EOnnxExecutionPreference
types.doc:
Where a session runs. FromConfig follows ml.ExecutionProvider; the others
pin one session regardless of it (a test comparing GPU against CPU output).

types.name: FOnnxDeviceInfo
types.doc: One device an execution provider offers in this process.

members.name: IsAvailable
members.doc:
False when the module compiled without a usable runtime (should not
happen — the build gates on the vendored binary) or the ORT
environment failed to come up.

members.name: RuntimeVersion
members.doc: The ONNX Runtime version string, for logs/diagnostics.

members.name: AvailableProviders
members.doc:
Execution providers compiled into the vendored runtime, CPU last. The
WebGPU provider is a plugin library and is listed by Devices() instead.

members.name: Devices
members.doc:
Every execution provider device the environment offers, plugin
providers included — the CPU always, a GPU when the WebGPU provider
registered and found an adapter.

members.name: HasGpuDevice
members.doc:
True when a GPU device is on offer. GpuUnavailableReason says why not
(provider library missing, failed to register, no adapter).

members.name: IsStarted
members.doc:
True once something in this process brought ONNX Runtime up. Every
query above starts it (and with it the GPU provider), which a UI that
only wants to describe the current state should not do.

members.name: SetExecutionPreference
members.doc: Set before a load; a loaded session keeps the device it loaded onto.

members.name: SetCpuUnderAuto
members.doc:
A model the GPU does not pay off for: Auto (the cvar's or this
session's) loads it on the CPU, an explicit Gpu still takes the GPU.

members.name: LoadFromMemory
members.signature: bool LoadFromMemory(const void* data, size_t size)

members.name: ExecutionProvider
members.doc:
The provider and device the loaded model runs on ("WebGpuExecutionProvider"
on "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 ..."); empty until loaded. Nodes the provider
has no kernel for still run on the CPU inside the same session.

members.name: InputNames
members.doc: Model I/O names in declaration order — empty until loaded.

members.name: Run
members.signature: bool Run(const std::string& inputName, const float* data, const std::vector<int64_t>& shape, const std::string& outputName, std::vector<float>& outData, std::vector<int64_t>& outShape)
members.doc:
Run one inference: a single float32 input tensor in, a single float32
output tensor out. `shape` is the input's dims (e.g. {1, 3, 512, 512});
the output's dims land in `outShape`. Returns false on any ORT error
(logged). Multi-input models bind by the given name.

members.name: LastError
members.doc: The last error message ORT reported, for tests/tools.

members.name: confidence
members.doc: Mean probability the model gave the characters it emitted, 0..1.

types.name: FSpeechRecognizer
types.doc:
FSpeechRecognizer — on-device speech to text: a CTC acoustic model run
through ONNX Runtime and decoded greedily. The engine ships
wav2vec2-base-960h (Apache-2.0, int8-quantized, Engine/Source/Runtime/ML/Models/ASR, packed into MLModels.meaf):
raw 16 kHz audio in, one of 32 characters per 20 ms frame out, which needs
no mel front end and no language-model search — what lets it run on a
game's spare core.

members.name: LoadFromMemory
members.signature: bool LoadFromMemory(const void* data, size_t size)

members.name: Transcribe
members.signature: bool Transcribe(const float* samples, size_t count, FSpeechTranscript& outTranscript)
members.doc:
Mono samples at 16 kHz, any scale (they are normalized here, as the
model's feature extractor does). False on an inference error.

members.name: Resample
members.signature: static void Resample(const float* samples, size_t count, uint32_t fromRate, std::vector<float>& outSamples)
members.doc: Linear resampling to 16 kHz.

members.name: DecodeCtc
members.signature: static std::string DecodeCtc(const float* logits, size_t frames, size_t vocabulary, float* outConfidence)
members.doc:
Greedy CTC over [frames x vocabulary] logits with the wav2vec2 alphabet:
repeats collapse, the blank drops, '|' is a space.

members.name: WordErrorRate
members.signature: static float WordErrorRate(const std::string& reference, const std::string& hypothesis)
members.doc:
Word error rate of a hypothesis against a reference, case and
punctuation ignored: (substitutions + deletions + insertions) / words.

members.name: Session
members.doc:
The model's session: set its execution preference before a load, read
the provider it landed on after.

members.name: energyThreshold
members.doc: RMS (of -1..1 samples) a 20 ms window needs to count as speech.

members.name: silenceSeconds
members.doc: Silence that ends an utterance.

members.name: maxSegmentSeconds
members.doc:
An utterance longer than this is cut and captioned, so a monologue
still shows up while it goes on.

members.name: minSpeechSeconds
members.doc: Shorter bursts are clicks and breaths, not words.

members.name: preRollSeconds
members.doc:
Audio kept from before the first loud window, so a soft first
consonant is not cut off.

types.name: FSpeechCaptioner
types.doc:
FSpeechCaptioner — turns streams of audio (one per speaker) into captions:
each stream is cut into utterances by energy, and every utterance is
transcribed — on a worker thread when async, so the game thread only ever
pushes samples and pops finished lines.

members.name: FSpeechCaptioner
members.signature: explicit FSpeechCaptioner(FSpeechRecognizer& recognizer, bool async = true)

members.name: Push
members.signature: void Push(uint32_t source, const float* samples, size_t count, uint32_t sampleRate)
members.doc: Any rate, mono, -1..1.

members.name: PushPcm16
members.signature: void PushPcm16(uint32_t source, const int16_t* samples, size_t count, uint32_t sampleRate)

members.name: Flush
members.doc:
Ends the source's current utterance now (a speaker who stopped talking
into push-to-talk, the end of a clip).

members.name: WaitIdle
members.doc: Blocks until every queued utterance is transcribed.

members.name: TileSize
members.doc:
Input pixels per tile edge and per feathered overlap. Zero picks the
model's default: 256 for the upscalers (a 1024 output tile), 512 for the
map generators.

members.name: Seamless
members.doc: Pad with the opposite edge (tiling textures) instead of the nearest one.

members.name: Load
members.signature: bool Load(ETextureEnhanceModel model, const std::vector<uint8_t>& onnxBytes)

members.name: Run
members.signature: ETextureEnhanceResult Run(const FTextureEnhanceImage& input, FTextureEnhanceImage& output, const FTextureEnhanceTiling& tiling, uint32_t outputDivisor, const FTextureEnhanceProgress& progress)
members.doc:
Upscalers keep the alpha channel (resampled) and apply `outputDivisor`
(1, 2 or 4) per tile, so a 4x pass whose result would exceed the output
budget lands at 2x or 1x without ever holding the full 4x image. Map
generators write opaque output: a unit normal in DirectX convention
(green points down the image, the engine's tangent basis), or grey
roughness / height.

members.name: Session
members.doc:
The model's session: set its execution preference before Load, read the
provider it landed on after.

members.name: MaxOutputSize
members.doc:
The upscaled texture's largest side never exceeds this; a source already
at or above it is left alone.

members.name: NormalPath
members.doc:
Empty skips that map. The caller picks the names so it can steer clear
of files an artist authored.

members.name: CanEnhance
members.doc: PNG, JPEG, TGA and BMP: the formats the job can write back in place.

members.name: MapPath
members.signature: static std::string MapPath(const std::string& sourcePath, ETextureEnhanceModel model)
members.doc: `<stem>_<suffix>.png` beside the source.

members.name: UpscaleDivisor
members.signature: static uint32_t UpscaleDivisor(uint32_t width, uint32_t height, uint32_t maxOutputSize)
members.doc:
1 for a full 4x upscale, 2 when only 2x fits `maxOutputSize`, 0 when not
even that does — a 1x pass would spend minutes to change nothing visible.

members.name: Run
members.signature: static FTextureEnhanceJobResult Run(const FTextureEnhanceRequest& request, const FTextureEnhancerProvider& enhancers, const FTextureEnhanceJobProgress& progress)

free.name: FTextureEnhanceProgress
free.doc: Called after every tile with the fraction done; returning false cancels.

free.name: FTextureEnhanceJobProgress
free.doc: Progress reports the overall fraction and a short label of the running step.

free.name: FTextureEnhancerProvider
free.doc:
Supplies loaded models, so a queue can keep sessions alive across jobs
instead of rebuilding a 30 MB graph per texture.
